topics: Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-11-12 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~47 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan, Priya, Mark (Redwood) / Samir, Claire, Derek, Ana (Maven)

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey team, thanks for carving time. Quick intros then we'll jump into current workload and targets.
[00:18] Samir (Maven Head ML): Hi all, Samir here. We run a combined chat + rec engine for support and product suggestions. Looking at moving inference out of a bunch of ad-hoc infra into a platform.
[00:32] Claire (CTO): Our big constraints are budget — we have a hard monthly cap for model ops — and data residency, so any hosted option needs to mitigate PII concerns.
[00:45] Jordan: Got it. Priya and Mark are with me — Priya will cover performance and batching, Mark on deployment options.
[00:50] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi everyone. To orient: we usually model unit cost as per-1000-token cost with levers like batching window, cache hit rate, quantization, and model choice.
[01:05] Ana (Product): Can you give a concrete example? We have peak chat at 3k qps and avg seq length ~140 tokens.
[01:12] Priya: Sure. Quick back-of-envelope: with hosted small model at 16-bit, without batching you're looking at X per 1k tokens — sorry thats shorthand — but with batching and 60% KV cache hit rate you can drop to ~30-45% of that. We'll send numbers.
[01:35] Derek (Infra): What's the difference if we go Dedicated? We want predictable costs and isolation.
[01:42] Mark (Redwood SE): Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput. With reserved capacity we can commit to latency SLOs and you often see better unit economics if your baseline qps justifies the commit. There is an upfront monthly commit vs pay-as-you-go for hosted.
[02:05] Samir: Our procurement team prefers reserved when it reduces headcount ops and cost variability. But can you quantify "better unit economics"?
[02:14] Priya: Yes. Example scenario: if you commit to a Dedicated pool sized for your 99th-percentile traffic, your per-token amortized infra cost can fall by 20-40% compared to hosted list price because we can pack longer batches and use KV cache more aggressively when you're the tenant.
[02:36] Claire: But what about data leaving our VPC? With Dedicated does data still route via Redwood control plane?
[02:44] Jordan: For Dedicated we offer network isolation and can do private peering. For Private (VPC/on-prem) the customer controls the network and keys. Hosted keeps things simplest but less control over residency. We'll attach the deployment matrix in the follow-up.
[02:58] Ana: Latency — we need p95 sub 200ms for simple chat completions. Is that achievable with batching?
[03:06] Priya: Yes, but batching introduces a tradeoff: larger batches increase throughput and lower cost per token but increase latency for individual requests. Our runtime supports dynamic batching with a latency cap; you can set a max wait time (e.g., 10ms-30ms) and a max batch size. For p95 <200ms on avg 140 tokens, should be fine if you tune the window.
[03:30] Samir: How about prefix/KV cache? We have a lot of repeated prompts for order status — can that be cached?
[03:38] Priya: Absolutely. Prefix caching — storing KV cache(s) for frequent prompt prefixes — can reduce the total tokens executed per request by serving from cache for initial layers. In practice, customers see 20-60% token reduction depending on repetition. The tricky part is cache invalidation for dynamic contexts.
[03:58] Derek: Is cache per-tenant? Any additional cost for cache storage?
[04:03] Mark: Cache is tenant-scoped in Dedicated/Private. For hosted there are per-tenant logical caches but we have retention policies. Storage costs are modest; the main saving is compute tokens avoided.
[04:20] Claire: For procurement we need a clear cost model. Can you show hosted list price vs committed Dedicated with an amortization?
[04:28] Jordan: We'll send a unit-econ spreadsheet. In short: hosted is simple per-token pricing + small infra overhead; Dedicated blends a monthly commit plus lower effective per-token billing when you exceed baseline.
[04:44] Ana: Any discounts for multi-region deployment? We need EU and NA presence for latency/residency.
[04:51] Jordan: Multi-region Reserved pools increase commit but reduce egress and cross-region latencies. We can show scenarios.

[05:10] --- technical interlude ---
[05:12] Priya: Quick Q on model choice: are you planning to run a single model for both chat and rec or two separate endpoints?
[05:18] Samir: Initially same model, but we might split later. We need to budget for inference and retraining.
[05:25] Priya: Splitting helps since recs can tolerate higher latency and lower-cost models; chat needs tighter p95. That helps unit cost a lot.

[06:00] Claire: Regarding security, SOC2 is required; we also need KMS control and SSO via SAML.
[06:08] Jordan: We support SAML SSO for the Console, KMS integrations for Private/Dedicated, and we can provide SOC2 attestations. We'll attach the security pack.
[06:20] Derek: For Private on-prem, what's the typical ops burden?
[06:25] Mark: Private gives max control but higher ops. We provide an install bundle and optional managed services. Many customers prefer Dedicated when they want isolation without full on-prem operational weight.

[07:05] Samir: Ok practical numbers — our traffic: baseline 800 qps, peak 3k qps, avg token 140, monthly budget hard cap $XXk (redacted here). Can you produce an option that fits under that cap?
[07:22] Priya: We'll map your QPS to GPU vCPU equivalents. For example with batching + cache and a 75% cache hit, the effective tokens executed could drop to ~35% of raw tokens. That pushes Dedicated cost lower. But if cache hit is low you may not get the same savings.
[07:45] Ana: How do you estimate cache hit realistically?
[07:48] Priya: We ask for sample traffic or logs; we can run a small pilot where we replay X% of traffic to estimate hit and latency impact.
[07:58] Jordan: That's part of the next step we proposed.

[08:12] --- mis-transcription/clarify noise ---
[08:15] Claire: Quick Q on tokenization — do you bill on input+output?
[08:19] Jordan: Yes, per-token billing counts prompt + generated tokens in hosted. For Dedicated, we still measure tokens but the per-token rate is generally lower because of commit amortization.
[08:32] Derek: What about low-level optimizations like quantization — do you manage that or do we need to provide a new model?
[08:40] Priya: We can deploy quantized variants — 8-bit/4-bit — depending on model compatibility. Some open models support that out-of-the-box; for custom models we run a quantization validation. That changes latency and sometimes quality; we'll show the tradeoffs.

[09:05] Samir: Can Redwood do canary rollouts during version swaps? We run nightly model updates.
[09:11] Mark: Yes — rollouts, A/B and automatic fallback policies are built-in. You can pin versions per route. This helps reduce regression risk which ties back to cost because you avoid big rollbacks.

[10:00] Ana: Any hidden fees — egress, storage, or long-tail costs?
[10:05] Jordan: Standard items: egress for multi-region flows, long-term KV retention beyond default, and enterprise support addons. We'll list them.

[10:32] Claire: If we choose Dedicated, is there an on-ramp? trial?
[10:36] Jordan: We often run a 4-week pilot on a small Dedicated slice or hosted pilot with a path to convert usage to Dedicated commit. The pilot includes basic perf runs and billing analysis.

[11:05] Priya: For the benchmark we'll need: sample prompts, traffic profile (qps by hour), sample latencies, and a list of top prompt prefixes for cache targeting.
[11:18] Samir: We'll get those.

[11:35] Mark: One more point on batching: we support continuous batching where the runtime builds batches opportunistically; you can set latency SLO and we respect it. Also, short tokens tend to pack efficiently; long sequences reduce batch density.
[11:55] Derek: For our infra team, who would we work with to set up VPC peering and KMS?
[12:02] Jordan: Derek — you'll work with our infra onboarding engineer; we'll CC them when arranging the pilot.

[12:20] Ana: Pricing nuance — is there a volume banding for tokens once you hit X tokens/month?
[12:27] Jordan: Yes, we have volume tiers and enterprise pricing for committed usage; the spreadsheet will show banded per-token rates.

[12:45] --- wrap-up and recap ---
[12:47] Jordan: Quick recap: Redwood to send unit-econ model + pricing scenarios (hosted vs committed Dedicated vs Private), security docs, and propose benchmark dates. Maven to send traffic samples and top prefixes.
[13:05] Claire: That works. If Dedicated gets us under the budget cap and meets residency, we'll push procurement.
[13:12] Samir: One ask — can you model three scenarios: conservative cache (20% hit), realistic (45%), optimistic (70%)?
[13:20] Priya: Yep we'll include those.
[13:28] Derek: I'll send our p95 goals and current infra diagrams.
[13:33] Jordan: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the attachments.
[13:40] Meeting ends.

Notes: transcript contains a few mis-heard words and shorthand; speakers occasionally overlap. Links shared: security pack (link in follow-up), unit-econ spreadsheet (will be shared).
